A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing material can be matched across relocation and renumbering; v3 adds an MSE appendix and expands the perceptron analysis.

before.justification: v2 reports original perceptron simulations and CNN, ResNet, and Vision Transformer experiments, including benchmark exponent estimates and robustness analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original perceptron and deep-network experiments and adds numerical results for an MSE-trained perceptron in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The logistic-loss perceptron procedure and spectral-complexity analysis of deep networks are unchanged. MSE is introduced as a comparison control, while the expanded derivation adds analysis rather than a proposed algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same teacher–student classification setting and MNIST, CIFAR10, and CIFAR100 image-classification coverage. The new MSE experiment explicitly retains the perceptron setting and changes only the loss.

E2.justification: v3 Appendix C adds an MSE-trained perceptron as a comparison with logistic/cross-entropy training. The classical learning-rule comparisons and existing optimizer and norm comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a matched-setting loss control, repeating the perceptron setup with MSE. Existing experiments retain their dataset-size grids, learning rate of 0.001, and 500-epoch CNN and 1000-epoch ResNet/ViT budgets.

E4.justification: New Appendix C and Figure 7 test whether the dynamical scaling laws depend on the loss function. Existing analyses of weight decay, optimizers, alternative norms, overparameterization, and training time remain.

E5.justification: Both retain the same description of up to 30 training repetitions, with five for the slowest model. Averaging, fitting uncertainties, and error propagation in v2 Appendix E/v3 Appendix F are unchanged; the MSE addition introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 Figure 7 adds MSE learning curves for alpha = 3.1, 6.25, 12.5, and 25, reported to lack the early power law and to have constant optimal norm across alpha. Tables 1–5 and all original plotted results are retained.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix C supported the perceptron exponent through numerical effective-slope curves. v3 Appendix D adds stationarity equations and an asymptotic derivation of epsilon proportional to (alpha lambda)^(-1/2), with validity range 1 << lambda << alpha, in Equations (14)–(21). Its printed potential has the opposite sign to Equation (1), creating an internal inconsistency.

C1.justification: The abstract and concluding contributions retain the same two dynamical scaling laws, their connection to end-of-training scaling, and the proposed relationship with implicit bias. New evidence and discussion support or qualify these retained claims.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly discusses loss dependence, offers margin normalization as a possible explanation for spectral complexity, and proposes predicting larger-dataset curve shapes while acknowledging that robustness validation is needed. It also expands the explanation for not varying model size. The principal interpretations and existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly identifies the computational platform as the DARIAH HPC-AI cluster at CNR-NANOTEC in Lecce. Core implementation information, GPU/CPU counts, training budgets, and the repository address remain unchanged. Moving the repository disclosure to the appendix does not establish changed resource availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds Caballero et al. on broken scaling laws, Li et al. on scaling-law methodology, Wei et al. and Schaeffer et al. on emergence, and Barbier et al. on multilayer-perceptron theory. These broaden context and future directions without substantially changing the novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Localized revisions clarify static versus dynamical learning curves and norm as training status, expand the introduction and discussion, and update affiliations and acknowledgements. Code availability moves to the appendix. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain.

P2.justification: v3 adopts ICLR typography and running headers throughout and substantially changes display sizes and placement. Figures 3 and 4, previously together on one page, appear enlarged on separate pages. A new Figure 7 is added; existing plot content and table structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: The MSE control and clearer applicability discussion strengthen the evidence and interpretation while preserving the original results. Appendix D adds an explanation of the exponent and its validity range, but its sign inconsistency with Equation (1) limits the theoretical gain. Together, these provide a limited net improvement rather than a substantial resolution of the paper's theoretical limitations.
